column2: At a road junction, in a cremation ground, in a river, at a river confluence, on an island, at a crossroads, in a mansion, house, lotus pond, on a mountain top,
at a burrow door, in an old well, an old house, a wall, among shigru, shleshmataka and akshe trees, jambu and udumbara,
in a banyan, an old rampart; on the mouth, heart, armpit or collarbone; palate, temple, throat, head, chin, navel and feet —
the bite is inauspicious. The auspicious messenger has flowers in hand, fair speech and good mind, is equal in sex-mark and color, in white clothes, clean and pure;
one who comes by a side door, armed, heedless, looking at the ground, in discolored clothes, with a noose in hand, with stammering speech;
one resting on dry wood, depressed, with hands and clothes smeared with sesame; with wet clothes, hair with black and red flowers;
one who rubs the breasts, cuts nails, touches the anus, scratches the foot, loosens hair, cuts grass — such messengers are bad, each alone.
If the Ida (breath) flows otherwise or in two ways for the messenger and oneself, by these two one should know the male, female and neuter nature of the patient.
Whichever limb the messenger touches, in that one should declare the bite. Moving of the messenger's feet is bad; standing motionless is good;
the messenger at the patient's side is auspicious; one coming from elsewhere bad. The patient is bad by going and coming; good at the messenger's report.
The messenger's speech is bad if it blames the earlier half; by the divided ends of his words, the timing of poison or no poison.
By the first vowels, and the ka-series, the script is divided in two kinds: vowel-born, and the group-letters... the Matrika.
Wind, fire, Indra and water are the four in the groups; the fifth letters are neuter; the vowels are of Indra and water origin.
The messenger's speech-feet are bad in wind and fire; the middle is Hari; the Varuna letters are praised; the neuters are very bad.
At departure, auspicious words, the thunder of cloud and elephant, circumambulation by a fruit tree, and the cry on the left conquered —
auspicious are songs and the like; the opposite is for failure. Cries of misfortune, chariot-noise, a cry on the right, a sneeze:
a courtesan, a sneezing king, a maiden, a cow, an elephant, drum and banner, milk, ghee, curds, conch, water, umbrella, kettle-drum, fruit, wine,
rice, gold and silver — these facing one are for success. One with wood, with fire, an artisan, wearing dirty clothes,
one with a throat-held axe, jackal, vulture, owl, cowrie; oil, skull and cotton — in prohibition; ash for destruction.

Poison diseases are seven, from the obtaining of one element after another. The poison bite goes to the forehead, then to the eye, then comfort; from the mouth it obtains the elements in order through the vein of speech.
By touching with the Tarkshya star one should destroy two poisons in the hand. In circles and the rest, the poets conquered those letters in the sky;
with the best two fingers at the joints at the navel-places of the body; from the knee gold-colored, from the navel snow-bright,
saffron-red to the neck, white from the hair-ends; Tarkshya pervading the cosmic egg, called Chandra, adorned with serpents,
the destroyer of the dark fierce, the Self, the great-winged — the wise should remember him. Thus from the words of the Tarkshya Self the mantra becomes the mantra-master's in poison.
The fist of the Tarkshya hand, the thumb standing inside, destroys poison. Having raised the Tarkshya hand, by moving its five fingers
one should make poison stop and the rest, by the word told. From the sky this is the earth-seed; the lord of five letters is the mantra.
Stop the poison — by that speech one would stop poison; with reversed adornments, the seed mantra, well accomplished.
Samplava, plavaya — Yama; from the sound it would remove poison; it raises the staff, by sprinkling with well-recited water;
or by hearing the sound of well-recited conch, kettle-drum and the like, it burns, joined, standing by reversal of the earth and fire elements.
By reversal of earth and wind this mantra transfers the poison. Standing within, in one's own house, with seed, fire, moon and water selves,
the mantra-master should do this work, with body in the form of Garuda; standing in the Tarkshya-colored house, by reciting it he destroys poison.
The Jamudandi told, marked with the Svadha and Shri seeds, by bathing and drinking conquers all poison, fever, affliction and untimely death.
Pakshi, Pakshi, Mahapakshi, Mahapakshi, vidhi svaha. Pakshi, Pakshi, Mahapakshi, Mahapakshi, kshi kshi svaha.

These two bird-king mantras destroy poison by consecration. "We know the bird-king; we meditate on the bird-god; may that Garuda impel us." Fire-standing, with side and former, the tusked and Shri-bearing and Dandin; Sakala and Langali — the Nilakantha and others are told; one should place white on chest, throat and crest, well refined, in the pillar.

Hara, Hara — homage to the heart; to Kapardin for the head; to Nilakantha the crest; to the eater of Kalakuta poison, svaha; then the armor and eye on the throat; the hide-clad, three-eyed, with faces to east and the rest of white, yellow, red and black; bearing fearlessness, boon, bow and Vasuki in his arms; his deity is Gauri-Rudra at the side.
Having placed the mantra-letters at feet, knees, loins, navel, heart, throat, face and head, and on the hands in the fingers beginning with thumbs,
to the forefinger and the ends one should place all in the thumbs. Having so meditated one should quickly remove it with the bound trident-mudra;
the little finger bound with the elder, three others spread, quick. In removal of poison, the left hand; in another, the right hand.

Om homage to the Lord Nilakantha, chih; to the stainless-throated chih; to the all-knowing-throated chih, throw, Om svaha; "to the stainless Nilakantha, remover of all poisons, homage to you, Rudra's wrath" — by this wiping the poison perishes without doubt; one should whisper in the ear or recite on sandals; one should worship Nilagriva Maheshvara by the Rudra rule; destruction of poison-disease follows having done the Rudra rite.
In the entire Rudra chapter the Vedic seer is also in the supreme ones. Prajapati of the gods, of Kutsa again of three,
of the two minds Uma is one; Rudra and the Rudras are the deities. The first anuvaka before is of the deity called Ekarudra;
the meter of the first is Gayatri, of three verses Anushtubh; of three likewise Pankti and Anushtubh are remembered;
of two the meter is Jagati; of the Rudras also eighty; three of Hiranyabahu, and "Namo vah kirikaya";
five verses are Rudra-deities in the mantra of the Rudra anuvaka; in the twentieth the Rudra deities: the first is remembered as Brihati;
the second Rik, three Jagati and Trishtubh; three Yajus of Anushtubh — one who knows the Arya and the rest attains good success.
Even with the Trailokyamohana, crushing poison and disease and enemies: "Im shrim hrim hraum hum — to Trailokyamohana Vishnu, homage." The Anushtubh of Narasimha destroys poison and disease:
Om im im — I bow to Ugravira, Mahavishnu, blazing, all-faced, Narasimha, terrible, death of death.
This alone, five-limbed, is the mantra accomplishing all aims. The twelve- and eight-syllable mantras crush poison and disease;
Kubjika, Tripura, Gauri, Chandrika, remover of poison; the Prasada mantra removes poison, increases life and health; the Saura, Vinayaka, likewise Rudra mantras are always entire.

Om homage to the Lord Rudra, lord of ghosts, gutta gutta, garja garja, bhramaya bhramaya, muncha muncha, muhya muhya, kata kata, avisha — the golden-bird Rudra commands, tha tha — this is the Patalakshobha mantra, destroying poison by recitation. In a bite of a snake and the like, one bitten by wood, stone and the like instantly
for pacification of poison should (cut or burn) the bite from the body with a flaming brand, red lotus and the like. Shirisha seed, flower, arka milk, seed, the three pungents
destroy poison by drinking, anointing, collyrium and the like. Pepper steeped in shirisha flower juice, white,
by drinking, nasal medicine, collyrium and the like destroys poison, no doubt. Koshataki, vacha, hing, shirisha, arka milk, joined,
the three pungents with equal water remove poison by nasal medicine and the like. Powder of ramatha, ikshvaku and sarvanga is an anti-poison nasal medicine;
indrabala, agnikandrona, tulasi, devika, saha — the three pungents powder anointed with their juice removes poison as food; the five parts of shirisha on dark fifth remove poison.
Its seed is to be taken by you, Brahma said to her. Having bowed to that herb, then throwing barley with the fist,
having repeated this mantra ten times one should salute the herb: "I raise you, upward-eyed" — and one should eat it with this.

Homage to Purushasimha; homage to Gopalaka. By the self alone one knows Krishna's defeat in battle;
agnipuran:296:20	by this true word may my antidote succeed. Homage to the Vaidurya-mother, tan tan, protect me from all poisons, Gauri, Gandhari, Chandali, Matangini, svaha, Harimaye. This mantra is to be applied at the beginning of medicines in stationary poison.
For one who has just eaten, standing in flames — lotus served with cold water — one should give with ghee and honey; if it is poison, immediately after.
With fish, meat, liquor, scents, garlands, incense and lamps; one should anoint with dhataki, lodhra, manjishtha, tala and sandal;
and fumigate with buffalo-eye; the fearsome seizer in two nights. Its signs: cough, breathing, repeated contraction of the limbs.
One should anoint with goat's urine, krishna, sevya, apamarga, sandal; fumigate with cow's horn, tooth and hair; the offering as before.
The seizer in three nights is Ghantali: its signs repeated crying, yawning, sounding, terror, limb-agitation, distaste.
One should anoint with kesara, anjana, cow's tusk and goat's milk; fumigate with nakhi, bilva leaves, and remove the offering.
The fourth seizer is Kakoli: limb-agitation and distaste, foaming, belching, gaze to directions; offering with kulmasha and asava.
Anoint with elephant tusk, snake slough and horse urine; fumigate with raji, neem leaf and shaken hair.
The fifth is "swan-excess": yawning, breathing in and up, clenching the fist; its signs; the offering should be removed with fish and the like.
One should anoint the child with ram's horn, bala, lodhra, shila and tala. The sixth seizer is Phatkari: fear, bewilderment, loud crying,
fasting, limb-throwing; one should remove the offering with fish and the like; by fumigation and anointing with raji, guggulu, kushtha, elephant tusk and the like.
In the seventh, loose-haired, afflicted, foul-smelling, yawning, depressed, crying, cough: fumigate with tiger claws and anoint.
With vacha, cow-dung and cow-urine; Shridandi is the eighth seizer: gazing at directions, moving the tongue, cough, crying;
the offering as before with fish and the like; for fumigation and anointing, hingula; the upward-seizing great seizer with vacha, mustard and garlic:
agitation, upward breathing, eating its own two fists; one should fumigate and anoint the child with red sandal, kushtha and the like.
Fumigation with monkey hair and nails; the tenth seizer is Rodani: its signs are constant crying, fragrance and blue color.
